intro: These anonymised examples describe the work delivered and the evidence behind it. Client details and unpublished results are kept private.

cases.title: A completion event was not a confirmed customer.
cases.completed: Completed: independent review, findings report and supporting evidence.
cases.question: Could website reporting reliably explain enquiries, customer registrations and payments?
cases.role: I reviewed the analytics and tracking configuration, compared website journeys with the business definitions, and tested selected behaviour in a controlled copy of the website.
cases.delivery: Some events described website activity rather than a dependable count of confirmed customers. The written audit distinguished accepted enquiries, customer confirmation and different payment categories. It set out the evidence, limitations and repairs to prioritise.
cases.context: A browser event alone could not establish every business outcome. The recommendations identified where operational records were needed and where tracking could be improved. The audit did not establish a revenue increase or a completed implementation.

cases.title: Separate websites. One reporting structure.
cases.completed: Completed: a dashboard with two reporting views and a definitions page.
cases.limitation: No quantified business-impact claim is made.
cases.question: How could the team understand website performance using a report that was useful for recurring reporting and governance questions?
cases.role: I developed the reporting dashboard and worked through the team’s questions about the metrics and their interpretation.
cases.delivery: The completed report brought the two website views into one location, with a separate definitions page. Feedback on the draft informed the explanation of the measures. A limitation in the available search-term history was explicitly recorded.
cases.context: The value was in the combination of a usable reporting view, clear definitions and documented source coverage. It shows completed reporting delivery for professional regulators without implying a wider government endorsement or claiming an unmeasured performance improvement.

cases.title: Portal tracking checked before release.
cases.completed: Completed: GTM configuration and GA4 validation in staging.
cases.limitation: The later production release is outside this example.
cases.question: An agency was updating a professional regulator’s practitioner portal and needed selected page and course activity recorded in GA4.
cases.role: I worked with the developer on the event requirements, configured the relevant GTM variables, triggers and tags, and checked their behaviour on the staging website.
cases.delivery: The selected events were confirmed as firing to GA4 in the test environment. The handover clearly identified that point of validation and the need for a further check when the agency released the update.
cases.context: Specialist tracking support can fit into an existing agency and development workflow. Clear communication about what has been tested is part of the deliverable.
